key_insight: Exciton transport in perovskite nanocrystal solids is governed more by energetic disorder than by structural disorder, so more monodisperse films can still transport excitons less efficiently.
engineering_relevance: Ligand-chain engineering can be used to tune nanocrystal disorder and improve optoelectronic device performance in LEDs, lasers, and solar cells.
method: Resolved exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy
Compared disorder effects across nanocrystal solids made with different alkylamine ligand lengths
Linked ligand-dependent size/shape polydispersity and quantum confinement to transport behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that longer alkyl-chain ligands produced more monodisperse but smaller nanocrystals with greater energetic disorder, and these solids showed less efficient exciton transport.
watch_item: The results come from solution-processed disordered nanocrystal films, so device translation may depend on controlling ligand chemistry, film morphology, and synthesis reproducibility.
paper_title: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
